steps.description: Design the optical layers of the display: backlight or emission layer, color filter, polarizer, and enhancement films for LCD; or emission stack and encapsulation for OLED.

inputs.name: technology-selection
inputs.desc: Display type and pixel architecture

inputs.name: performance-specification
inputs.desc: Target brightness, contrast, gamut, viewing angle

outputs.name: optical-stack-design
outputs.desc: Layer-by-layer specification: for LCD (backlight: LED type, light guide, diffuser, prism sheets, DBEF, polarizer, LC cell, color filter, cover glass); for OLED (substrate, TFT, OLED stack: HIL/HTL/EML/ETL/EIL, cathode, thin-film encapsulation, cover)

outputs.name: optical-performance
outputs.desc: Luminance uniformity, angular luminance distribution, spectral output, power efficiency (lumens per watt of electrical input)

process: For LCD backlight: edge-lit (LEDs along one or more edges of a light guide plate) for slim form factor. Direct-lit (LED array behind the panel) for local dimming with high dynamic range. Mini-LED backlight: thousands of small (100-200um) LEDs for fine-grained local dimming (1000+ dimming zones) to approach OLED-like contrast.

Backlight optical films: diffuser (homogenizes the light from the light guide), BEF (brightness enhancement film: prismatic sheet that recycles off-axis light, increasing on-axis brightness by 1.5-1.8x), DBEF (dual brightness enhancement film: reflects one polarization back for recycling, increasing polarized output by 1.3-1.5x). Total backlight efficiency from LED to panel: 5-8% of electrical power becomes screen luminance.

For OLED emission stack: the organic layers are deposited by vacuum thermal evaporation (small molecule) or inkjet printing (polymer). Stack order: anode (ITO) / HIL (hole injection) / HTL (hole transport) / EML (emissive layer: host + dopant) / ETL (electron transport) / EIL (electron injection) / cathode (thin metal or transparent). For white OLED (WOLED) in large panels: stack blue + yellow-green emitters, use color filter array for RGB subpixels.

OLED encapsulation: organic materials degrade in the presence of moisture and oxygen. Thin-film encapsulation (TFE): alternating layers of inorganic (Al2O3, SiNx by ALD or PECVD) and organic (polymer by inkjet). WVTR (water vapor transmission rate) target: < 1e-6 g/m^2/day. Edge seal with desiccant for additional moisture protection.

For micro-LED: each pixel is an individual LED chip (InGaN for blue/green, AlInGaP for red). Mass transfer from epitaxial wafer to display backplane is the key manufacturing challenge. Approaches: pick-and-place (slow but proven for large pixels), stamp transfer (elastomer stamp picks up arrays), laser lift-off + fluidic self-assembly. Defect management: redundant sub-pixels or post-transfer repair by laser.

steps.description: Calibrate the display color output and implement color management: gamma correction, white point, gamut mapping, and uniformity compensation.

inputs.name: optical-stack-design
inputs.desc: Spectral output of the display at each primary color

inputs.name: optical-performance
inputs.desc: Measured luminance and chromaticity across the panel

outputs.name: color-calibration
outputs.desc: 3x3 color matrix (display RGB to XYZ), gamma curves per channel, white point (CCT and chromaticity), color accuracy (average and maximum delta-E 2000 across a test patch set)

outputs.name: uniformity-compensation
outputs.desc: Per-pixel or per-zone gain and offset corrections to achieve luminance uniformity < 5% and chrominance uniformity < delta-u'v' 0.005 across the panel

process: Characterize the display: measure the spectral power distribution of each primary (R, G, B) and white at multiple drive levels (0-255 in 8-bit). From the spectra, compute the CIE 1931 XYZ tristimulus values. The chromaticity of each primary defines the display's color gamut triangle on the CIE diagram.

Gamma calibration: the electro-optical transfer function (EOTF) relates the digital input value to the luminance output. Measure L(digital_value) for each channel. For sRGB: the EOTF is approximately gamma 2.2 with a linear segment near black. For HDR (PQ/ST 2084): the EOTF is perceptual quantizer, mapping code values to absolute luminance up to 10,000 nits. Build a 1D LUT per channel to correct the native gamma to the target EOTF.

White point: target D65 (6504K) for most applications. Measure the native white point and compute the 3x3 matrix to transform from display RGB to D65-referenced XYZ. Apply this matrix in the display controller or GPU. For cinema (DCI-P3): white point is D63 (6300K, slight green shift from D65).

Gamut mapping: when the source content gamut exceeds the display gamut, out-of-gamut colors must be mapped to the nearest displayable color. Perceptual mapping (compress the entire gamut proportionally) for photo/video. Relative colorimetric (clip only out-of-gamut, preserve in-gamut) for proofing. Compute delta-E 2000 for the 24 patches of the ColorChecker chart: target average delta-E < 2.0 for a calibrated display, < 1.0 for a reference monitor.

Uniformity compensation: measure the luminance and chromaticity at a grid of points (9x9 minimum) at full white and at 50% gray. Compute the correction gain and offset for each zone to equalize the output. For OLED: per-pixel aging compensation tracks the cumulative usage of each sub-pixel and adjusts the drive current to compensate for differential degradation (the blue sub-pixels degrade faster than red and green).
